slides.title: Polynomials
slides.speaker_notes: Sums of powers of x with nice coefficients — and the deep link between zeros and coefficients.

slides.title: What you'll be able to do
bullets: State the degree of a polynomial and classify it.
Define a zero and verify by substitution.
Use α + β = −b/a, αβ = c/a for quadratics.
Build a quadratic from its zeros.
Divide one polynomial by another and verify p = g·q + r.

slides.title: What is a polynomial?
bullets: p(x) = a_n x^n + … + a_1 x + a_0 with real coefficients.
Degree = highest power of x with non-zero coefficient.

slides.title: Zeros (roots) of a polynomial
bullets: A zero is a value c with p(c) = 0.
Linear ax + b: exactly one zero, x = −b/a.
Quadratic ax² + bx + c: 0, 1 or 2 real zeros.
A polynomial of degree n has AT MOST n real zeros.

slides.title: Discriminant and the parabola
bullets: For ax² + bx + c, discriminant D = b² − 4ac.
D > 0 → two distinct real zeros (parabola crosses x-axis twice).
D = 0 → one repeated zero (parabola TOUCHES x-axis).
D < 0 → no real zeros (parabola lies entirely above or below).

slides.title: Build a quadratic from its zeros
bullets: Given sum S and product P, a quadratic with those zeros is x² − S·x + P.
Zeros 3 and −2: S = 1, P = −6 → x² − x − 6.
Surd zeros come in conjugate pairs (rational coefficients).
Multiply by any non-zero constant for an equivalent polynomial.

slides.title: Polynomial long division
bullets: Given p(x), g(x) with deg g ≤ deg p, find q(x), r(x) with p = g·q + r.
Stop when the running remainder has degree < deg g.

slides.title: Find a missing zero by division
bullets: x³ − 4x² + x + 6 has 2 and −1 as zeros.
Use known zeros + division to extract the rest.

slides.title: You try (5 minutes)
bullets: 1. Sum and product of zeros of 2x² − 7x + 3.
2. Build a quadratic with zeros 4 and −1.
4. Discriminant of x² − 4x + 4 — what does the graph look like?
5. Divide x³ − 1 by x − 1; state quotient and remainder.

slides.title: Key takeaways
bullets: Polynomial: a_n x^n + … + a_0; degree = highest power.
Zero: p(c) = 0 ↔ x − c is a factor; geometric x-intercept.
Division algorithm: p = g·q + r with deg r < deg g — verify after dividing.
